name: Amancio Ortega
title: The Billionaire Who Never Had an Office
subtitle: A railway worker's son becomes an errand boy in a shirt shop, then founds Zara and Inditex, and somehow stays almost invisible the whole way.
hook: By the late 1990s his clothes were sold around the world, yet no photograph of Amancio Ortega had ever been published. The first one appeared in Inditex's first annual report in ==1999==, a plain shot of a serious man in a white shirt and dark jacket. Before that, there were rumours that the founder of Zara **did not even exist**.

glance.label: Born
glance.value: 28 March 1936, Busdongo de Arbas, a hamlet of about 60 people in León, northern Spain, just as the Spanish Civil War began

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: Youngest of four children; his father worked on the railway and his mother was a housemaid. The family moved to A Coruña in Galicia and lived in a row house beside the train tracks

glance.label: School and first job
glance.value: Left school at about 14. Started as an errand boy, then a shop hand, at a shirt shop in central A Coruña (Gala), where he learned the clothing trade

glance.label: First company (age)
glance.value: Confecciones GOA, a small workshop making quilted bathrobes, opened in 1963 when he was 27; his brother ran sales and his sister kept the books

glance.label: First Zara store (age)
glance.value: 1975 in A Coruña, aged about 39, two blocks from the shirt shop where he started; opened with his then-wife Rosalía Mera

glance.label: Main company today
glance.value: Inditex (Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius, Oysho, Zara Home, Lefties). He controls about 59.3% of its voting rights through Pontegadea Inversiones (50.01%) and Partler Participaciones (9.28%), and has sat on its board since June 1985

glance.label: Net worth
glance.value: $144.9 billion, #11 in the world (Forbes real-time estimate, 29 October 2026); source: Zara, self-made

glance.label: Family (public basics)
glance.value: Married to Flora Pérez Marcote, who chairs his foundation and sits on the Inditex board; three children. Daughter Marta Ortega Pérez has chaired Inditex since 2022

glance.label: Giving
glance.value: Fundación Amancio Ortega (created 2001). Its €310 million programme (2015–2025) put about 450 cancer-diagnosis and treatment machines into Spain's public hospitals

contact.howToReach: Amancio Ortega has no social media at all: his own foundation says so in writing, so any account using his name is fake. He almost never gives interviews and no channel reaches him personally, but his companies publish real doors: journalists can write to press@inditex.com, shareholders to ir@inditex.com or accionistas@inditex.com, and Zara shoppers with an order problem should use Zara's own customer care (its verified Instagram points to @zaracare). Do not pitch a startup or ask for money: the Fundación Amancio Ortega says it does not finance private initiatives and that neither Ortega nor its chair Flora Pérez ever asks anyone for money or gives investment tips, so treat any such message as a scam. The one open application is the foundation's scholarship for a school year in the US or Canada, and it is only for students in Spain. If you do write to Inditex, send three or four sentences in English or Spanish: who you are, the one thing you want, and why it matters to their business.

factCheck.method: Profile built on 29 October 2026 from Inditex's own contact, history, board and shareholder pages; the Fundación Amancio Ortega's contact, project and scholarship pages; Forbes' real-time profile; Fortune's 2013 profile; Spanish press (El Debate, El Español). Wikipedia was used only as a lead to find sources. Social accounts were checked on the live profile pages; Ortega has none of his own, which the foundation states in writing. Photos come from Wikimedia Commons with licence and author read through the Commons API.

disputed.claim: When the family moved to A Coruña
disputed.note: Fortune (2013) says the family moved when he was small; El Español (2026) says he was 12; Wikipedia says 14 and that he spent his early childhood in Tolosa (Basque Country). We avoid giving an exact age for the move.

disputed.claim: His first job and the age he started
disputed.note: Fortune says he was barely a teenager when he became a shop hand at Gala and that he chose to leave school at 13; El Español says he left school at 14 and began as an errand boy before becoming a shop assistant. We say 'about 14' and list both roles.

Fortune and El Debate agree no photo of him was published until 1999 (El Debate: in Inditex's first annual report). Other accounts describe his first public appearance in 2000, ahead of the 2001 stock-market listing. Both can be true; we use the 1999 photo.

disputed.claim: Has he ever given an interview?
disputed.note: Some reports say he has never given a formal interview; others say he has spoken to only a handful of journalists, notably his biographer Covadonga O'Shea. We say only that he almost never gives interviews.

Forbes says he co-founded Inditex with his then-wife Rosalía Mera (died 2013) in 1975; Inditex's own history names Ortega as founder and dates Inditex itself to 1985, with the first Zara store in 1975. We say he opened the first Zara store with Rosalía Mera.

Wikimedia Commons has one image of Ortega (File:Amancio-ortega.300w.webp, 300×407 px) marked 'own work, CC BY-SA 4.0' by a one-time uploader. Its size and file name look like a resized image copied from a website, so we doubt the licence and did not use it. Portrait is left empty.
The Instagram handle @inditex is not verified, had six followers when checked and links to a Telegram channel. It is not an official Inditex account and is left out.
